name: Question 1
problem:
Given that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

 express the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}$ in terms of the components of $y.$
worked_solution:
First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

gives the following expressions for ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & ={x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2} & ={x}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

By solving the second equation for ${x}_{1}$ and substituting it into the first equation, we obtain the following expressions for ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={y}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} & =-{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute these into our quadratic form expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & ={x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & ={y}_{2}^{2}+2{y}_{2}(-{y}_{1}+{y}_{2})+(-{y}_{1}+{y}_{2})^{2} \\  & ={y}_{2}^{2}+-2{y}_{2}{y}_{1}+2{y}_{2}^{2}+{y}_{1}^{2}-2{y}_{2}{y}_{2}+{y}_{2}^{2} \\  & ={y}_{1}^{2}-4{y}_{1}{y}_{2}+4{y}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Given that [y1y2]=[1−110][x1x2], express the quadratic form Q(x)=x12+2x1x2+x22 in terms of the components of y.

a
y12−2y1y2+2y22
b
y12+2y1y2+2y22
c
y12−2y1y2+y22
d
y12−6y1y2+y22
e
y12−4y1y2+4y22
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that

[y1y2]=[1−110][x1x2]

gives the following expressions for y1 and y2:

y1=x1−x2y2=x1

By solving the second equation for x1 and substituting it into the first equation, we obtain the following expressions for x1 and x2:

x1=y2x2=−y1+y2

Now, we substitute these into our quadratic form expression:

Q(x)=x12+2x1x2+x22=y22+2y2(−y1+y2)+(−y1+y2)2=y22+−2y2y1+2y22+y12−2y2y2+y22=y12−4y1y2+4y22
